hypothesis.title: valkey-cart blocked by long-running Lua script causing BUSY errors and 800ms latency
hypothesis.summary: A long-running Lua script in valkey-cart is blocking the Redis instance, causing "BUSY Redis is busy running a script" errors and 1650ms slow queries. Valkey-cart CPU spiked to 97% of limit and p95 latency jumped from 3ms to 808ms. This propagates upstream: cart and checkout calls fail with BUSY errors, and frontend p95 latency rose from 182ms to 717ms, triggering the alert.
hypothesis.reasoning: The alert fired on frontend latency, but frontend is a victim here. Trace analysis shows valkey-cart accounts for 100% of the added latency (+541ms). The evidence chain is clear: valkey-cart logs show "BUSY Redis is busy running a script" errors starting 16 minutes before the alert, with slow queries of 1650ms. Valkey-cart's p95 latency spiked from 3ms to 808ms at the same time (-15m), and CPU jumped from ~9% to 97% of limit. The "BUSY" error is a Redis-specific message indicating a long-running Lua script is blocking the server. This is not a client-side pool exhaustion issue (PM-2026-03-12 pattern) because we see the errors and latency directly in valkey-cart's own logs and metrics, and the CPU saturation is on the valkey-cart server itself. The mechanism is datastore_degradation: a slow or pathological script is monopolizing the Redis instance, causing both high CPU and blocking other commands. The deployments of recommendation and shipping at -33m are red herrings—they are not on the critical path (frontend→cart→valkey-cart) and their own metrics show no issues. Valkey-cart's request rate is stable, so this is not a load spike; something changed in the query pattern or a script was introduced.

supporting_evidence.why_it_matters: 1,152 BUSY errors in valkey-cart confirm a long-running script is blocking the Redis server, starting 16 minutes before the alert.
3,456 slow queries averaging 1650ms show the script is monopolizing CPU and blocking other commands.
CPU jumped from 9% to 97% at -15m, coinciding with the latency spike, indicating the script is CPU-intensive.
Valkey-cart p95 latency spiked from 3ms to 808ms at -15m, proving the datastore itself is degraded, not just client-side issues.
Trace analysis confirms valkey-cart is the origin of 100% of added latency (+541ms) in frontend traces, ruling out other dependencies.
280 frontend errors calling cart with the same BUSY message show the problem propagates upstream through the call graph.

suggested_actions.title: Inspect and kill the blocking Lua script in valkey-cart
suggested_actions.command: kubectl -n otel-demo exec deploy/valkey-cart -- valkey-cli SCRIPT KILL
suggested_actions.rationale: SCRIPT KILL will terminate a running Lua script that has not yet written data. This is the safest immediate mitigation if the script is read-only. If it fails (script already wrote), you may need to restart the pod.

suggested_actions.title: Check the slowlog to identify the offending script
suggested_actions.command: kubectl -n otel-demo exec deploy/valkey-cart -- valkey-cli SLOWLOG GET 20
suggested_actions.rationale: The slowlog will show the exact Lua script or command causing the 1650ms queries, helping identify the root cause (e.g., a new feature or data pattern).

suggested_actions.title: Restart valkey-cart to immediately clear the blocking script
suggested_actions.rationale: If SCRIPT KILL fails or the script has already written data, a restart will forcibly clear the blocking script and restore service. This will briefly interrupt cart operations.

alternatives.why_less_likely: PM-2026-03-12 describes a client-side pool exhaustion pattern, but here we see the errors and latency directly in valkey-cart's own metrics and logs, with CPU at 97%. The problem is server-side, not client pool limits.

retrieved_documents.title: Cart / Valkey errors and timeouts
retrieved_documents.snippet: Decide whether the problem is the client pool or the server. - Server: `kubectl -n otel-demo exec deploy/valkey-cart -- valkey-cli --latency` and `SLOWLOG GET 10`. High latency or `BUSY` => datastore degradation. - Client: server latency flat but cart logs `pool busy=N/N` or "timeout awaiting connection" => pool exhaustion. Raise the pool size and restart cart.
